newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African platinum mine work stoppage.
newsitem.headline: South African platinum mine work stoppage.

text.p: South Africa's Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd said on Wednesday that it had an illegal work stoppage at the Amandelbult section of its Rustenburg mine.
The problem started when employees at two Amandelbult workers hostels took illegal industrial action over the Friday sacking of an employee.
The workers did not turn up for Monday's night shift and a fight broke out at one of the hostels between strikers and employees who wanted to work.
"Mine management intervened and ended the confrontation. One employee was seriously injured," Amplats said in a statement.

"Management condemns the illegal work stoppage and the intimidation and violence which it caused. Management will take the necessary action, in consultation with the SAPS (police) and the NUM to ensure the safety of all workers," the firm added.

The statement gave no details of the size of the disturbance or whether it had hit production, but media reports said 4,600 workers at Amandelbult had joined the stoppage and hit 20 percent of platinum production.
Precious metals dealers in New York said the news had increased nervousness in the already tight platinum market.

Rustenburg has a current production capacity of 1.3 million ounces of platinum a year. Last year a bitter and unofficial strike at the mine lead to the loss of 100,000 ounces of platinum production and the dismissal of 28,000 workers.
